name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline. It sharpens fine details in low-res frames without hallucinating artifacts, which directly lifts EXCAVA’s output quality. The trade-off is a 10-15% slowdown in upscaling speed, but the gain in detail clarity outweighs the latency for high-stakes renders.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal artifact, not a spatial one. The real risk is wasting time on a 10-15% slowdown for zero motion-quality gain. Instead, test VFI-Flow’s temporal interpolation first; if it cuts motion blur by even 0.5%, that’s the 0.5% capability jump we need.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add VFI-Flow to EXCAVA’s motion pipeline. It reconstructs motion blur into sharp frames by filling gaps between existing frames, which directly attacks the core temporal artifact Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 20-30% increase in compute per clip, but the gain in motion clarity—even 0.5%—outweighs the cost because EXCAVA’s output is judged on motion fidelity first. Depth-aware upscaling can wait; blur kills perceived quality faster than soft edges.

name: Torque
text: VFI-Flow’s 20-30% compute hit is a gamble—EXCAVA’s temporal bottleneck isn’t blur, it’s temporal *artifacts* like ghosting or strobing from frame blending. Test a lightweight temporal denoiser first (e.g., RIFE’s clean mode) to see if it trims artifacts without the compute tax; if it fails, then push VFI-Flow—but only after proving the bottleneck is motion blur, not corruption.

name: Dynamo
text:
DECISION: Hybrid pipeline—run VFI-Flow only on keyframes with worst motion blur, then let EXCAVA’s existing denoiser handle the rest; RIFE clean mode tests first to confirm temporal artifacts aren’t the bottleneck.

Result: EXCAVA’s motion clarity improves by ≥0.5% with minimal compute waste. Owner: Torque.
